fact: The Minister of Security and Civil Protection chairs Guinea's national SIPAO steering committee, and Guinea has signed a memorandum with INTERPOL and the decrees creating and organising the Centre de Recueil et d'Enregistrement des Données Policières (CREDPOL), per the ministry's account of the 30-31 March 2021 regional steering committee.

The minister told the regional steering committee on 31 March 2021 that a budget line for SIPAO was already in the Ministry of Security and Civil Protection's 2021 budget; the equipment itself (40 computers, 40 routers, 40 scanners, 2 servers) was a European Union donation through INTERPOL.

The ministry states, as an intention and not as something in operation, that the national database will handle procedures along the penal chain and allow all procès-verbaux drawn up in the services to be digitised.

Ten police and gendarmerie units of Greater Conakry had been equipped with the SIPAO kit by 31 March 2021, with other services to follow, and 44 police and gendarmerie officers trained as trainers and users, per the ministry; no total of units is given and the document does not say the units were yet entering records.
